fl-q1.text: Classify the leak (TM para 2-7). Class I: wetness or discoloration, not enough to form drops. Class II: drops form but do not drip from the item. Class III: drops form and FALL from the item.

options.label: Class I — wetness or discoloration only
Class II — drops form but do not fall
Class III — drops fall from the item

fl-q2.text: Class I or II leak. Operation is allowed EXCEPT for the brake system. Identify the fluid by its location and appearance. Brake fluid is silicone (BFS); it is found at the master cylinder, brake lines, or at a wheel/brake. Note: Type 2 coolant is also purple, so use location to tell them apart.

options.label: Brake fluid (master cylinder, brake lines, wheel/brake area)
Not sure whether it is brake fluid
Coolant (green, pink, or purple; sweet odor) — radiator, hoses, surge tank
Transmission, transfer case, or power steering fluid (Dexron VI, red)

fl-q3.text: Class III leak. Is it brake fluid, or is it coming from a loose fitting, connector, or hose clamp that you can tighten? CAUTION: Do not tighten transfer case oil cooler retaining nuts (internal damage may result) and do not attempt to repair brake fittings.

options.label: Loose fitting, connector, or hose clamp (not brake, not transfer case oil cooler)
Other source, or no loose fitting found

fl-a1.text: Tighten the loose fitting or clamp
fl-a1.actionText: TM para 2-6/2-7: if a fitting or connector is loose, tighten it; if broken or defective, report it. Tighten the loose hose clamp or fitting. Wipe the area dry, run the engine if needed, and re-check the leak class after a few minutes.

fl-q5.text: After tightening and wiping dry, what is the leak class now?

options.label: No leak, or only Class I/II

fl-q4.text: Which fluid has the Class III leak?

options.label: Transmission, transfer case, or power steering fluid (Dexron VI)

fl-t-brake.text: Any brake fluid leakage must be reported (TM para 2-7). Do not operate. Notify unit maintenance.

terminal.summary: Brake fluid leak — NMC (TM para 2-7; PMCS items 1/3/4/6/34)

fl-t-doubt.text: WHEN IN DOUBT, NOTIFY YOUR SUPERVISOR (TM para 2-7). Treat as a possible brake fluid leak — do not operate until your supervisor or unit maintenance confirms it is not brake fluid.

terminal.summary: Leak of unidentified fluid, possible brake fluid — NMC pending supervisor check

fl-t-cool12.text: Class I/II coolant leak — operation allowed. Check coolant level more frequently and record on DA Form 2404.

terminal.summary: Class I/II coolant leak — operation allowed, monitor level

fl-t-oil12.text: Class I/II engine oil leak — operation allowed. Check oil level more frequently and record on DA Form 2404.

terminal.summary: Class I/II engine oil leak — operation allowed, monitor level

fl-t-dex12.text: Class I/II transmission/transfer/power steering fluid leak — operation allowed. Check fluid levels more frequently and record on DA Form 2404. Do not tighten transfer case oil cooler retaining nuts.

terminal.summary: Class I/II Dexron fluid leak — operation allowed, monitor level

fl-t-fuel12.text: Class I/II fuel leak — operation allowed. Keep sparks and flame away, monitor the leak, and record on DA Form 2404.

terminal.summary: Class I/II fuel leak — operation allowed, monitor

fl-t-fixed.text: Leak corrected by tightening the loose fitting/clamp. Recheck the fluid level and monitor during operation.

terminal.summary: Class III leak at loose fitting/clamp — tightened, now Class I/II or none

fl-t-cool3.text: Class III coolant leak. Report immediately to your supervisor or unit maintenance. Do not operate.

terminal.summary: Class III coolant leak — NMC

fl-t-oil3.text: Class III oil leak. Report immediately to your supervisor or unit maintenance. Do not operate.

terminal.summary: Class III engine oil leak — NMC

fl-t-dex3.text: Class III transmission/transfer/power steering fluid leak. Report immediately. Loss of power assist can occur with a power steering Class III leak (PMCS item 32). Do not operate.

terminal.summary: Class III Dexron fluid leak (trans/transfer/power steering) — NMC

fl-t-fuel3.text: Class III fuel leak. Report immediately to your supervisor or unit maintenance. Do not operate.

terminal.summary: Class III fuel leak — NMC

tmReference: TM 9-2320-387-10, Table 1-15/1-15.1 (tire pressure); Table 2-2 items 2, 5, 24, 28, 39; para 3-25

options.label: Penetrating object (nail, metal, etc.) in tread
Lug nut or stud nut loose, broken, or missing
Excessive inner/outer wear or out of balance

td-q2.text: Is any tread worn even to the height of the tread wear indicator/wear bar (1/16 in. (1.59 mm) or less)?

options.label: Yes — tread is flush with the wear bar
No — tread is above the wear bar

td-a1.actionText: Inflate to TM Table 1-15 (Load Range D) or Table 1-15.1 (Load Range E), TM page 1-12.1. M1151/M1152 — Load Range D: unloaded 20 psi front / 20 psi rear; at GVW 30 front / 40 rear. Load Range E: unloaded 18 front / 25 rear; at GVW 30 front / 45 rear. M1151A1/M1152A1 (incl. W/B1, W/B2), either load range: unloaded 35 front / 45 rear; at GVW 40 front / 50 rear. Mud, sand, and snow (30 mph max): 20 front / 30 rear. Unloaded = driver plus one passenger. Never exceed 50 psi cold. Load Range D and E valves/tires/wheels are not interchangeable. Gauge the tire with a tire inflation gauge.

td-q3.text: Does the tire hold pressure after inflation?

td-a2.actionText: Remove all penetrating objects (PMCS items 24/28). Then check the tire for air loss with a tire gauge.

td-q4.text: Does the cut, gouge, or crack extend to the cord body, or is there any bulge?

options.label: Yes — reaches the cord body, or a bulge is present
No — surface damage only, cord body not exposed

td-q5.text: Is any wheel stud nut or lug nut broken or missing, or only loose?

td-a3.actionText: Tighten loose lug nuts (para 3-25) and have unit maintenance tighten stud nuts and lug nuts to proper torque (PMCS item 39b).

td-t1.text: Tire missing, deflated, or will not hold air. Replace with the spare (para 3-25) or notify unit maintenance.

terminal.summary: Tire deflated/missing/will not hold air — NMC (PMCS items 2/5/24/28)

td-t2.text: Cut, gouge, or crack to the cord body, or a bulge — tire is unserviceable.

terminal.summary: Tire cut to cord body or bulge — NMC (PMCS item 39a)

td-t3.text: Tread worn to the wear bar — tire is unserviceable.

terminal.summary: Tire tread worn to wear indicator — NMC (PMCS item 39a)

td-t4.text: Tread is wearing but still above the wear bar. Note on DA Form 2404 and monitor.

terminal.summary: Tire tread wearing, above wear bar — monitor

td-t5.text: Tire inflated to TM pressure and holding.

terminal.summary: Low tire pressure — inflated per TM Table 1-15/1-15.1, holding

td-t6.text: Tire exhibits excessive inner and outer wear or balance problem.

terminal.summary: Excessive inner/outer tire wear or balance — NMC (PMCS item 39a)

td-t7.text: Surface damage that does not reach the cord body. Record on DA Form 2404 and monitor.

terminal.summary: Tire surface cut/gouge, cord body not exposed — monitor

td-t8.text: A wheel stud nut or lug nut is broken or missing.

terminal.summary: Wheel stud/lug nut broken or missing — NMC (PMCS item 39b)

td-t9.text: Loose lug nuts tightened. Unit maintenance must torque stud nuts and lug nuts.

terminal.summary: Loose lug nuts tightened — maintenance to torque

ws-q1.text: Turn the rotary switch to RUN, wait for the wait-to-start lamp to go out, then turn to START. What happens?

options.label: Engine cranks at normal speed but does not start

ws-q2.text: Is the transmission shift lever in P (park)?

options.label: No — it was in another position

ws-a1.text: Place the shift lever in P
ws-a1.actionText: Place the transmission shift lever in P (park) and try to start again.

ws-q4.text: Does the engine crank and start now?

ws-q3.text: Remove the companion seat. Check battery fluid level and battery cable connections for looseness, damage, or corrosion (Table 3-1, malfunction 1, step 2). Do any of these conditions exist?

options.label: Yes — low fluid, or loose/damaged/corroded connections
No — fluid level and connections are OK

ws-q5.text: Attempt to slave-start the vehicle (para 2-23). Does the engine start?

options.label: Yes — engine starts with slave cable

ws-q6.text: Engine cranks slowly. Check battery fluid level and battery cable connections for looseness, damage, or corrosion (Table 3-1, malfunction 2, step 1). Do any of these conditions exist?

options.label: Yes — low fluid, or loose/damaged/corroded connections
No — fluid level and connections are OK

ws-q7.text: Attempt to slave-start the vehicle (para 2-23). Does the engine start?

options.label: Yes — engine starts with slave cable
No — still cranks slowly or will not start

ws-q12.text: With the engine running, check the voltmeter (PMCS item 12d). Does the needle stay in the yellow or red range?

options.label: No — needle is in the green
Yes — needle stays in yellow or red

ws-q8.text: Engine cranks normally but does not start. Does the fuel gauge indicate E (empty)?

ws-a4.actionText: Fill the fuel tank (para 3-21) and start the engine (para 2-12).

ws-q10.text: Does the engine start after fueling?

ws-q9.text: Did you wait for the wait-to-start lamp to go out before cranking (para 2-12)?

options.label: Yes — waited, still will not start

ws-a5.actionText: Turn rotary switch to RUN and wait until the wait-to-start lamp goes out (shade the lamp from sun glare). Turn to START and release when the engine starts. Above 0°F (-18°C) do not operate the starter continuously for more than 20 seconds; wait 10 to 15 seconds between attempts with the rotary switch left in RUN. If the switch was turned to ENG STOP after an unsuccessful start, wait 90 seconds before trying again (para 2-12).

ws-q11.text: Does the engine start using the correct procedure?

ws-a6.text: Purge the fuel system of air
ws-a6.actionText: Para 3-11b: Raise and secure hood. Disconnect fuel line from fuel filter outlet. Place a rag over the fuel filter outlet. Crank engine until rag is wet with fuel. Connect fuel line to fuel filter outlet. Start engine (para 2-12) and ensure fuel system has been purged of air. Lower and secure hood.

ws-q13.text: Does the engine start after purging the fuel system?

ws-q14.text: Does the wait-to-start lamp fail to light, or fail to go out (Table 3-1, malfunction 3, step 3)?

options.label: Yes — lamp does not light or does not go out

ws-t1.text: Engine started. Cause was operator procedure.

terminal.summary: Engine start issue resolved — operator procedure corrected

ws-t2.text: Engine started by slave-start and voltmeter is in the green. Batteries are weak — notify unit maintenance.

terminal.summary: Engine will not start without slave-start (PMCS 12b) — batteries weak, maintenance to check

ws-t3.text: Engine will not start even with slave power. Notify unit maintenance.

terminal.summary: Engine will not start (slave-start failed) — NMC (PMCS item 12b)

ws-t4.text: Engine started after fueling. Monitor fuel level.

terminal.summary: Engine would not start — out of fuel, refueled

ws-t5.text: Engine cranks but will not start after fueling/purging checks. Other causes — notify unit maintenance.

terminal.summary: Engine cranks, no start — NMC (PMCS item 12b), needs maintenance

ws-t6.text: Low battery fluid or loose, damaged, or corroded battery connections. Per Table 3-1, notify unit maintenance.

terminal.summary: Engine will not start — battery fluid/cable condition, maintenance required (PMCS item 12b)

ws-t7.text: Voltmeter needle stays in yellow or red range. Shut down and notify unit maintenance.

terminal.summary: Slave-started, voltmeter in yellow/red — NMC (PMCS item 12d)

ws-t8.text: Engine started after purging air from the fuel system.

terminal.summary: Engine would not start — fuel system purged of air (para 3-11)

ws-t9.text: Wait-to-start lamp fails to light or does not go out. Notify unit maintenance.

terminal.summary: Engine will not start — wait-to-start lamp fault (PMCS item 12a/12b)

tmReference: TM 9-2320-387-10, Table 3-1, Malfunctions 4 and 9; Table 2-2 items 10.1, 12, 16, 21, 35-37; para 3-14

el-q1.text: What electrical problem are you seeing?

options.label: Voltmeter shows not charging / loss of voltage
Hot water personnel heater fails to produce heat
Lights, horn, wipers, or washer inoperative
Air conditioner inoperative or not cooling
AFES control module or fire sensor LED not steady green
Gauge inoperative (oil pressure, coolant temp, voltmeter, speedometer)

el-q2.text: Check battery cable connections for looseness, damage, or corrosion (Table 3-1, malfunction 4, step 1). Any found?

el-q3.text: Check for broken or missing drivebelt (Table 3-1, malfunction 4, step 2).

el-q5.text: Check the heater operating controls for correct settings (Table 3-1, malfunction 9). Were they set wrong?

options.label: Yes — controls were not set correctly
No — set correctly, still no heat

el-a2.actionText: Set the heater controls correctly with the engine at operating temperature and wait a few minutes for heat.

el-q6.text: Is the heater producing heat now?

el-q7.text: Which item is inoperative? (TM Table 2-2 lists no not-mission-capable criterion for lights, horn, or wipers; vehicle operation with them inoperative may violate AR 385-55.)

el-a3.actionText: Para 3-14: Check fluid level in the washer reservoir; fill with water and cleaning compound per Table 3-2 if needed. If the washer does not work, check washer nozzles for dirt/debris and clear with fine wire. Check hoses for leaks or poor condition.

el-q8.text: Do the wipers and washer work now?

el-q9.text: Do climatic conditions require air-conditioning for the mission (PMCS item 21)?

el-q10.text: Is a fire sensor LED blinking/off only because the sensor is covered with dust or a foreign object?

options.label: Yes — sensor is dirty or covered
No — LED fault with clean sensor, or control module LED fault

el-a4.actionText: Remove the dust or foreign object from the optical fire sensor (TM caution: optical fire sensors must be kept clean). Then turn the rotary switch to RUN and recheck the control module and sensor LEDs.

el-q11.text: Are the control module LED and all sensor LEDs now continuous (steady) green?

el-t2.text: Drivebelt broken or missing — notify unit maintenance.

terminal.summary: Not charging — drivebelt broken/missing, NMC (PMCS item 7)

el-t3.text: Vehicle not charging — other causes. Notify unit maintenance.

terminal.summary: Not charging — NMC (PMCS items 12d/16e)

el-t4.text: Heater does not produce heat. Notify unit maintenance.

terminal.summary: Hot water personnel heater inoperative — needs maintenance

el-t5.text: Heater working after correcting control settings.

terminal.summary: Heater — controls corrected

el-t6.text: Battery cable connections loose, damaged, or corroded. Notify unit maintenance.

terminal.summary: Not charging — battery cable connections loose/damaged/corroded, NMC (PMCS items 12d/49)

el-t7.text: Light inoperative. No NMC criterion in TM Table 2-2 item 35; inoperable headlights may violate AR 385-55 — check unit/local policy before operating at night.

terminal.summary: Light(s) inoperative — PMCS item 35, needs maintenance

el-t8.text: Horn inoperative. No NMC criterion in TM Table 2-2 item 36; may violate AR 385-55.

terminal.summary: Horn inoperative — PMCS item 36, needs maintenance
Washer serviced (para 3-14) — wipers/washer working

el-t10.text: Wipers or washer still inoperative. No NMC criterion in TM item 37b-d; may violate AR 385-55.

terminal.summary: Wipers/washer inoperative — PMCS item 37, needs maintenance

el-t11.text: AFES control module LED is off/blinking or a fire sensor LED does not come on or blinks.

terminal.summary: AFES LED fault — NMC (PMCS item 10.1e/f)

el-t12.text: Gauge inoperative. Coolant temperature gauge inoperative (12h), voltmeter not indicating, or speedometer needle not moving/stuck (16g) are NMC. Shut off engine and notify unit maintenance.

terminal.summary: Instrument gauge inoperative — NMC (PMCS items 12/16)

el-t13.text: A/C inoperable and climatic conditions require air-conditioning. Record on DA Form 2404.

terminal.summary: A/C inoperable, climate requires A/C — NMC (PMCS item 21)

el-t14.text: A/C inoperable but not required for current climatic conditions. Record on DA Form 2404.

terminal.summary: A/C inoperable, not required by climate — needs maintenance (PMCS item 21)

el-t15.text: AFES sensor cleaned; all LEDs steady green.

terminal.summary: AFES fire sensor cleaned — LEDs steady green

un-q1.text: Where is the unusual noise or vibration coming from? (PMCS item 19: unusual noise or vibration from the engine, transmission, transfer, differentials, propeller shafts, axle shafts, or wheels is NMC.) For smoke or rough running use 'Exhaust Smoke'.

options.label: Engine, transmission, transfer, differentials, propeller shafts, or axle shafts
Exhaust — loud exhaust or exhaust leak
Brakes — grinding/squealing, or brakes pull or grab
Loose stowed equipment, tiedowns, or body panel rattle

un-q2.text: Check the wheel lug nuts (Table 3-1, malfunction 19, step 1). What do you find?

options.label: One or more lug/stud nuts broken or missing

un-a1.actionText: Tighten loose lug nuts (para 3-25) and notify unit maintenance to properly torque lug nuts.

un-q3.text: Inspect for mud or dirt buildup inside the rims (step 2). Is there buildup?

un-a2.actionText: Remove any mud or dirt buildup from inside the rims.

un-q4.text: Check tires for proper inflation pressure (step 3; Table 1-15/1-15.1). Are pressures correct?

options.label: No — one or more tires low

un-a3.actionText: Inflate to TM Table 1-15 (Load Range D) or Table 1-15.1 (Load Range E), TM page 1-12.1. M1151/M1152 — Load Range D: unloaded 20 psi front / 20 psi rear; at GVW 30 front / 40 rear. Load Range E: unloaded 18 front / 25 rear; at GVW 30 front / 45 rear. M1151A1/M1152A1 (incl. W/B1, W/B2), either load range: unloaded 35 front / 45 rear; at GVW 40 front / 50 rear. Mud, sand, and snow (30 mph max): 20 front / 30 rear. Unloaded = driver plus one passenger. Never exceed 50 psi cold. Load Range D and E valves/tires/wheels are not interchangeable.

un-q5.text: Drive the vehicle. Is the wobble/shimmy gone?

un-a4.actionText: Inspect stowage brackets, footman loops, tiedowns, and straps for security of mounting, damage, and missing components (PMCS item 51). Secure any loose stowed equipment.

un-q6.text: Is the noise gone after securing loose items?

options.label: No — noise remains / source not confirmed

un-t1.text: Wobble/shimmy corrected. If lug nuts were tightened, unit maintenance must torque them.

terminal.summary: Wheel wobble/shimmy corrected (lug nuts/rim debris/tire pressure)

un-t2.text: Wheels still wobble or shimmy — other causes. Notify unit maintenance.

terminal.summary: Wheel wobble/shimmy persists — NMC (PMCS items 18/19)

un-t3.text: A wheel stud nut or lug nut is broken or missing.

terminal.summary: Wheel stud/lug nut broken or missing — NMC (PMCS item 39b)

un-t4.text: Unusual noise or vibration from the powertrain. Notify unit maintenance.

terminal.summary: Powertrain unusual noise/vibration — NMC (PMCS item 19)

un-t5.text: Exhaust leak or damaged exhaust. Notify unit maintenance.

terminal.summary: Exhaust leak/damage — NMC (PMCS item 40)

un-t6.text: Brakes pull or grab, or unusual noise at the wheels/brakes. Notify unit maintenance.

terminal.summary: Brake pull/grab or brake/wheel noise — NMC (PMCS items 17/19)

un-t9.text: Rattle eliminated by securing stowed equipment.

terminal.summary: Rattle — loose stowed equipment secured

un-t10.text: Noise remains and cannot be confirmed as non-powertrain. Treat as PMCS item 19 and notify unit maintenance.

terminal.summary: Unusual noise, source not isolated — NMC (PMCS item 19)

eo-q1.text: Engine overheats according to the coolant temperature gauge. Is the radiator fan running?

eo-a1.actionText: The fan normally activates above 220°F (104°C) and deactivates at 190°F (88°C). Raise and secure hood (para 3-9). STOP the engine before disconnecting the time delay module. Disconnect the time delay module connector from the control valve connector. Start engine. Check fan for continuous operation; if the fan is not operating continuously, stop engine and notify unit maintenance. Lower and secure hood.

eo-q1a.text: Does the fan now operate continuously?

eo-q2.text: Allow engine to cool and check the coolant surge tank level (para 3-10). Is it at the COLD FILL LINE?

eo-a2.actionText: WARNING: Use extreme care removing the surge tank filler cap if the temperature gauge reads above 165°F (74°C); do not add coolant to a hot engine unless the engine is running; add slowly. Place a thick cloth over the cap, turn to the first stop to vent pressure, then push down and remove. Add coolant to the COLD FILL LINE. Do not mix Type 1 (green) and Type 2 (purple). Run engine one minute, stop, recheck; repeat until level stays at COLD FILL LINE. Install cap.

eo-q2a.text: After adding coolant and running the engine, does the coolant temperature stay at or below 250°F (120°C)?

eo-q3.text: Check for debris blocking the radiator fins (Table 3-1, malfunction 7, step 3).

eo-a3.actionText: With engine stopped, remove debris (mud, leaves, etc.) from the radiator fins without bending the fins. (Table 3-1 refers to para 3-26, which has been deleted from the TM.)

eo-q3a.text: After clearing debris, does the temperature stay at or below 250°F?

eo-q4.text: Check for broken or missing drivebelt (step 4).

eo-t1.text: Fan will not run even with the override. Stop engine and notify unit maintenance.

terminal.summary: Overheating — fan inoperative after para 3-23 override, NMC

eo-t2.text: Temperature normal after adding coolant. Check for leaks and monitor the gauge; record on DA Form 2404.

terminal.summary: Overheating — coolant low, added per para 3-10, temperature normal

eo-t3.text: Temperature normal after removing radiator debris.

terminal.summary: Overheating — radiator debris removed

eo-t4.text: Drivebelt broken or missing. Stop engine and notify unit maintenance.

terminal.summary: Overheating — drivebelt broken/missing, NMC (PMCS item 7)

eo-t5.text: Engine still overheats — other causes. Notify unit maintenance.

terminal.summary: Overheating — cause undetermined, NMC (PMCS items 12h/16c)

eo-t6.text: Emergency fan override performed. Allow engine to cool at idle to 185-250°F (85-120°C), then proceed to unit maintenance with the vehicle and tell them the emergency override was performed (para 3-23 h-i).

terminal.summary: Fan clutch failed — emergency override performed (para 3-23), proceed to maintenance

tmReference: TM 9-2320-387-10, Table 3-1, Malfunction 8; para 3-18; Table 2-2 items 12c, 16b, 31

op-q1.text: Low engine oil pressure. Stop the engine. Check the oil level (engine off, para 3-18). What do you find?

options.label: Oil level between ADD and FULL

op-a1.actionText: Remove oil filler cap and add engine oil (appendix G) to bring the level to the crosshatch marks between FULL and ADD 1 QT. Do not overfill. Use a non-vented filler cap only. Start engine and check oil pressure.

op-q2.text: After adding oil, is oil pressure at least 6 psi (41 kPa) at idle and 15 psi (103 kPa) under load (Before check, item 12c) — or, while driving, at least about 30 psi (207 kPa) under normal driving and 10 psi (69 kPa) at idle (item 16b)?

op-t1.text: Oil pressure normal after adding oil. Check for leaks; record on DA Form 2404.

terminal.summary: Low oil pressure — oil added per para 3-18, pressure normal

op-t2.text: Oil pressure low with proper oil level. Do not operate. Notify unit maintenance.

terminal.summary: Low oil pressure — NMC (PMCS items 12c/16b)

op-t3.text: Engine oil appears milky. Notify unit maintenance.

terminal.summary: Engine oil milky — NMC (PMCS item 31)

tr-q1.text: What transmission or transfer case problem are you experiencing?

options.label: No response to shift lever movement
Fluid thrown from transmission fill tube
Transfer case shift lever will not shift
Shift lever binds between detents / will not engage all ranges

tr-a1.text: Place lever in P and select transfer range
tr-a1.actionText: Check to see if the transmission lever is in P (park). Place transmission shift lever in P and select transfer gear range (Table 3-1, malfunction 10).

tr-q2a.text: Does the transmission respond to the shift lever now?

tr-a2.actionText: Secure the transmission dipstick. Wipe up spilled fluid.

tr-q3a.text: Has fluid stopped being thrown from the fill tube?

tr-q4.text: Check the fluid level for overfilling (para 3-19). Is the level above the crosshatch marks?

tr-q5.text: Check for low transmission fluid level (para 3-19). Is it low?

tr-a3.actionText: With engine running and service brake depressed, move the shift lever through all ranges and R, then check in N with parking brake applied. At operating temperature fluid should be at the crosshatch marks. Add Dexron VI (appendix G) through the fill pipe. Do not overfill.

tr-a4.actionText: Ensure the proper transfer case shifting sequence is used (para 2-13).

tr-q7.text: Does the transfer case lever shift now?

terminal.summary: Transmission slips — NMC (PMCS item 20)

tr-t2.text: No response to shift lever. Notify unit maintenance.

terminal.summary: Transmission will not shift — NMC (PMCS item 20)
Transmission/transfer issue corrected by operator

tr-t4.text: Transmission fluid level is high. Notify unit maintenance (an over-full transmission can indicate a transfer case fluid leak — PMCS item 22).

terminal.summary: Transmission overfilled / fluid thrown from fill tube — needs maintenance

tr-t5.text: Transmission light stays on. Notify unit maintenance — transmission damage can result if the cause is not determined (para 2-12 note).

terminal.summary: Transmission light on — needs maintenance

tr-t6.text: Rough shifting — all causes: notify unit maintenance.

terminal.summary: Rough shifting — needs maintenance (no NMC criterion if it shifts and does not slip)

tr-t7.text: Fluid thrown from fill tube with secure dipstick and normal level — other causes. Notify unit maintenance.

terminal.summary: Fluid thrown from transmission fill tube — needs maintenance

tr-t8.text: Shift lever inoperable, binds between range detents, or transfer lever does not engage all ranges.

terminal.summary: Shift lever inoperable/binds — NMC (PMCS items 11/21.2)

tr-t9.text: Transfer case shift lever will not shift — other causes. Notify unit maintenance.

terminal.summary: Transfer lever will not shift — NMC (PMCS item 11b)

tmReference: TM 9-2320-387-10, Table 3-1, Malfunctions 15-18; para 3-13; Table 2-2 items 12f, 14, 16f, 17, 34, 54

bi-q1.text: What brake problem are you experiencing?

options.label: Brakes will not stop the vehicle / poor service braking
Parking brake does not hold the vehicle
Parking brake lever safety mechanism does not latch
Brake fluid leak, or master cylinder cover missing
Parking brake actuating lever or spring broken or missing

bi-q2.text: Is the parking brake partially applied?

bi-q3.text: Is the brake warning lamp now off?

bi-a1.text: Clean and adjust the parking brake (para 3-13)
bi-a1.actionText: a. Chock wheels and release parking brake handle by depressing the safety release button. b. Turn adjusting knob clockwise as tightly as possible by hand. c. Apply parking brake handle. d. If it cannot be applied, turn knob counterclockwise until it can. e. Test: remove chocks, depress service brake and start engine, transfer in H and transmission in D, slowly let up on service brake — parking brake should hold the vehicle. f. (S/N 299999 and below) After mud or sand, clean actuating lever and spring with low-pressure water.

bi-q4.text: Does the parking brake hold the vehicle now?

bi-t1.text: Brakes will not stop the vehicle. Do not operate. Notify unit maintenance.

terminal.summary: Poor service braking — NMC (PMCS item 14a)

bi-t2.text: Service brakes dragging — all causes: notify unit maintenance.

terminal.summary: Service brakes dragging — needs maintenance

bi-t3.text: Brake warning lamp stays on with parking brake released. Notify unit maintenance.

terminal.summary: Brake warning lamp stays on — NMC (PMCS items 12f/16f)

st-q0.text: What steering problem are you experiencing?

options.label: Excessive free play, shimmy, sway, or unstable handling
Vehicle wanders to one side on level pavement
Movement at steering gear mounting when wheel is turned

st-q1.text: Check tires for proper inflation pressure (Table 3-1, malfunction 22, step 1). Any tires low?

options.label: Yes — one or more tires low

st-a1.actionText: Inflate to TM Table 1-15 (Load Range D) or Table 1-15.1 (Load Range E), TM page 1-12.1. M1151/M1152 — Load Range D: unloaded 20 psi front / 20 psi rear; at GVW 30 front / 40 rear. Load Range E: unloaded 18 front / 25 rear; at GVW 30 front / 45 rear. M1151A1/M1152A1 (incl. W/B1, W/B2), either load range: unloaded 35 front / 45 rear; at GVW 40 front / 50 rear. Mud, sand, and snow (30 mph max): 20 front / 30 rear. Unloaded = driver plus one passenger. Never exceed 50 psi cold. Load Range D and E valves/tires/wheels are not interchangeable.

st-q2.text: Check the power steering reservoir for low fluid level (para 3-20 for P/N RCSK 18330; para 3-20.1 for P/N 94252A sightglass). Is it low?

st-a2.actionText: Add steering fluid (appendix G; Dexron VI). RCSK 18330: level between HOT and COLD (warm) or ADD and COLD (cool). P/N 94252A: center of sightglass cold, top of sightglass hot. Do not overfill; keep dirt out. Check for leaks (PMCS item 32).

st-q2a.text: Is steering normal after adding fluid?

st-q3.text: Check for broken or missing drivebelt (step 3).

st-q4.text: Check the power steering oil cooler for bent fins or other air flow obstructions (step 4).

st-a3.actionText: Remove obstructions from the power steering oil cooler (fins not damaged).

st-q5.text: Check tires for proper inflation pressure (Table 3-1, malfunction 21). Any tires low?

st-a4.actionText: Inflate to TM Table 1-15 (Load Range D) or Table 1-15.1 (Load Range E), TM page 1-12.1. M1151/M1152 — Load Range D: unloaded 20 psi front / 20 psi rear; at GVW 30 front / 40 rear. Load Range E: unloaded 18 front / 25 rear; at GVW 30 front / 45 rear. M1151A1/M1152A1 (incl. W/B1, W/B2), either load range: unloaded 35 front / 45 rear; at GVW 40 front / 50 rear. Mud, sand, and snow (30 mph max): 20 front / 30 rear. Unloaded = driver plus one passenger. Never exceed 50 psi cold. Load Range D and E valves/tires/wheels are not interchangeable.

st-t1.text: Corrected by inflating tires to TM pressure.

terminal.summary: Steering/handling corrected — tires inflated per Table 1-15/1-15.1

options.label: Excessive exhaust smoke after engine reaches 185-250°F (85-120°C)
Engine starts but misfires, runs rough, or lacks power
Air restriction gauge in red zone

es-q3.text: Check engine oil level for overfilling (engine off, para 3-18). Is the level above FULL?

es-a4.text: Recheck for oil cooler drain-back (para 3-18 note)
es-a4.actionText: Operate engine for one minute, shut down, wait one minute, and recheck oil level.

es-q8.text: Does the oil level still check above FULL?

options.label: No — now between ADD and FULL

es-q4.text: Check for restricted air cleaner. Is the air restriction indicator in the red zone?

es-a2.actionText: Raise and secure hood. Start engine. Place the toggle fuel switch in the UP position and drain approximately 1 pt (0.47 L) of fuel into a suitable container. Place the switch DOWN when draining is complete. Stop engine. Lower and secure hood.

es-q6.text: Was the fuel clear after draining 1 pt, and does the engine now run smoothly?

options.label: Yes — fuel clear and engine runs normally
Fuel not clear after draining 1 pt
Fuel clear but engine still misfires/rough

es-a3.actionText: Check the air restriction gauge. If it is in the red zone: if an emergency situation exists, clean the air cleaner element (para 3-15: remove element, tap gently with hand, open end down; never strike on a hard surface; reinstall; notify unit maintenance to torque/set clamp). If no emergency exists, notify unit maintenance.

es-q7.text: Is the air restriction indicator in the red zone?

es-t2.text: Air cleaner restricted (indicator in red zone). Clean only as an emergency procedure (para 3-15); notify unit maintenance.

terminal.summary: Air cleaner restricted — NMC (PMCS items 12e/16d)

options.label: Ran out of fuel / air in fuel system, engine cranks but will not start

fs-a1.actionText: Shut off engine. No smoking, flame, or sparks. Remove fuel cap (do not over-turn the handle). Insert nozzle into the filler neck rubber cone without puncturing the strainer and fill. Install fuel cap and turn handle clockwise to seal. Start engine.

fs-a2.actionText: Raise and secure hood. Disconnect fuel line from fuel filter outlet. Place a rag over the fuel filter outlet. Crank engine until rag is wet with fuel. Connect fuel line to fuel filter outlet. Start engine and ensure the fuel system has been purged of air. Lower and secure hood.

fs-a3.actionText: Start engine. Place the toggle fuel switch UP and drain approximately 1 pt (0.47 L) into a suitable container, then place the switch DOWN. Stop engine.

fs-q3.text: Was the fuel clear after draining, and does the engine run smoothly?

options.label: Fuel not clear after draining 1 pt
Fuel clear but engine still rough
Class I or II (no drops falling)

terminal.summary: Fuel empty — tank filled (para 3-21)

cs-q1.text: What is the cooling system issue?

options.label: Fan, fan pulley, fan shroud, or radiator mounts/brackets damaged

cs-a1.actionText: WARNING: Use extreme care removing the surge tank filler cap if the temperature gauge reads above 165°F (74°C). Place a thick cloth over the cap, turn to the first stop to vent pressure, then push down and remove. Add coolant to the COLD FILL LINE (do not mix Type 1 green and Type 2 purple). Run engine one minute, stop, recheck; repeat until level stays at COLD FILL LINE. Install cap.

options.label: Class I or II (no drops falling)

cs-q2.text: Where is the Class III coolant leak?

options.label: Loose hose clamp at a hose-to-fitting connection
Radiator, hose itself, or other location

cs-a2.actionText: TM para 2-7: if a fitting or connector is loose, tighten it. Tighten the clamp, make sure the hose is fully seated, wipe dry, and observe for several minutes with the engine running.

cs-q3.text: After tightening, what is the leak class?

options.label: No leak, or only Class I/II

cs-a3.actionText: With the engine stopped, remove debris (mud, leaves, etc.) from the radiator fins without bending them (Table 3-1, malfunction 7, step 3).

cs-t1.text: Coolant at COLD FILL LINE. If the level drops again, look for a leak and notify unit maintenance.

terminal.summary: Coolant low — added per para 3-10

cs-t2.text: Leak stopped or reduced to Class I/II after tightening the clamp. Monitor.

terminal.summary: Coolant leak at hose clamp — tightened

cs-t3.text: Class III coolant leak. Report immediately. Do not operate.

terminal.summary: Class III coolant leak — NMC (PMCS items 33/48b)

cs-t4.text: Radiator debris removed. Monitor the coolant temperature gauge.

terminal.summary: Radiator fins cleared of debris
